audit_findings.title: Dockers may leave the owner-earnings numerator on the wrong perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $34.2 million FY2025 discontinued-operations loss before disposal gain and taxes; $139.0 million disposal gain; owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Dockers operating cash flows could alter the $232.5 million OE anchor, while any unpurged disposal gain could also affect OE; sale proceeds belong only in the balance-sheet bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Consolidated statements of cash flows include the cash flows from continuing and discontinued operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that consolidated cash flow combines continuing and discontinued operations, but it does not demonstrate that the OE calculation failed to remove Dockers. Dockers produced a $34.2 million pre-gain, pretax loss in FY2025, a meaningful scale relative to the anchor, although accounting loss does not establish its cash contribution. The cash-flow statement separately reverses the disposal gain, so gain double counting is not demonstrated. Direction remains mixed until the bridge is traced.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2025 OE from filed cash-flow lines, separately identify Dockers cash flows and transaction costs, confirm the $139.0 million gain was excluded, and restate all historical OE years on a continuing-operations perimeter before rerunning scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The bridge treats all cash and short-term investments as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $977.8 million gross bridge addition, equal to 24.0% of $4,068.0 million base equity value and $2.35 per share; $717.1 million of cash was held by foreign subsidiaries
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for operations, restricted, tax-burdened, or committed to obligations must be removed from the excess-cash equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Of our $757.9 million in cash and cash equivalents, approximately $591.9 million was held by foreign subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The full $977.8 million addition is demonstrated, while its full distributability is not. The exposure is material: complete exclusion would reduce base value from $9.79 to approximately $7.44 per share, and even partial exclusion could materially change reported intrinsic value and the buy-below price. Foreign location alone does not prove unavailability, but $717.1 million held abroad shows that the unresolved amount is large.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the May 31, 2026 cash and short-term investments to unrestricted excess cash after minimum operating liquidity, repatriation taxes, legal restrictions, Dockers-related commitments, and other transaction obligations; rerun every scenario with the verified excess-cash amount.

audit_findings.title: Finance leases may create an economic cost omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $73.5 million present-value finance-lease liability and $13.4 million filed 2026 lease payment; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If finance-lease ROU amortization is added back without deducting leased-asset consumption or replacement investment, OE and its capitalized DCF value are overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: In the first quarter of 2025, the Company recorded an additional Financing lease ROU asset and lease liability of $ 61.6 million in “Other non-current assets” and “Other long-term liabilities” balances on the consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The finance leases and their payment obligations are demonstrated, but omission from OE is not. The $73.5 million liability is only 1.8% of base equity value, yet a recurring missing asset-consumption charge would enter the OE numerator every year and could have a larger capitalized effect. The record does not identify the amortization included in OE or the maintenance-capex treatment, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile finance-lease ROU amortization, interest, principal payments, noncash additions, and leased-asset replacement requirements to the OE bridge; rerun OE only if amortization was added back without an offsetting maintenance charge.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded employee-benefit claims may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $55.2 million total net unfunded claims, equal to $0.13 per share and 1.4% of $4,068.0 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Net pension, postretirement, and deferred-compensation deficits are senior claims that reduce the equity bridge if not already captured elsewhere.
audit_findings.evidence: We have substantial liabilities and cash requirements associated with our postretirement benefits, pension, and deferred compensation plans.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed pension and postretirement deficits total $42.1 million, and deferred-compensation liabilities exceed Rabbi-trust assets by $13.1 million, for $55.2 million combined. Deducting the full amount would reduce base value from $9.79 to about $9.66 per share and bull value from $11.13 to about $11.00, leaving both far below the $21.06 market price. This is a demonstrated bridge omission if no equivalent deduction exists, but it is not material to the valuation conclusion at the filed scale.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the $107.7 million Rabbi-trust assets are not separately included in cash, deduct only the $55.2 million net unfunded amount if absent, and document the approximately $0.13-per-share bridge adjustment.

audit_findings.title: Restructuring may be recurring rather than safely disappearing after the anchor year
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.6 million FY2025 restructuring and related charges and $21.4 million H1 FY2026 restructuring charges; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash restructuring and transformation costs affect the OE anchor and projected growth-period OE if added back or assumed to disappear despite continuing recurrence.
audit_findings.evidence: We may incur additional significant restructuring and restructuring related charges as we progress the global productivity initiative, which could be material in a future fiscal quarter or year.
audit_findings.explanation: Recurrence is supported by $24.5 million of FY2025 restructuring charges, $12.1 million of related charges, and another $21.4 million in the first half of FY2026. These amounts are meaningful relative to the $232.5 million anchor. However, the record does not show whether the OE bridge retained or excluded the cash portions, and the filed totals include noncash impairments and other components. A valuation error therefore remains possible but is not demonstrated or quantifiable.
audit_findings.action: Trace severance, consulting, distribution-transition, contract-termination, incentive, impairment, and asset-sale items through the OE bridge; separate cash from noncash amounts and rerun the forecast with recurring transformation cash costs retained rather than automatically normalized away.
